title: Order lifecycle
description: An order moves through payment, packing, and delivery. Scenarios cover repeated payment notices, declined payments, delivery retries, and returns. See how saved payment records prevent duplicate work and how parcel records retain failed attempts and final delivery or return outcomes.

methods.description: Mark the order paid after its payment is captured.
Record successful capture of the authorized payment.
Record an issuer decline and its failure reason.
Increment the delivery attempt count and record any delivery issue.
Record the return reason and move the parcel into the returned state.

participants.label: Authorized customer payment awaiting settlement and capture

scenarios.title: New payment queues fulfillment
scenarios.description:
In this synthetic example, a gateway sends a new authorized-payment callback for pending order ORD-1042. The service verifies the receipt, captures EUR 89.90, and queues one fulfillment item. The recording ends with the order paid and ready for packing.

The shared domain groups commerce records, payment messages, and an external payment gateway. Gateway and message definitions illustrate integration boundaries; their instances are outside this recording’s captured state.

occurrences.changeSummary: Receipt rcpt-481 is created and linked to payment pay-72. The order and payment remain pending.
occurrences.narration: A callback arrives for order ORD-1042. The service creates a receipt for evt_481. No payment or fulfillment work has been completed yet.
The receipt has not been handled. The callback says the issuer authorized EUR 89.90, so this traversal takes the new-successful-callback branch.

occurrences.changeSummary: The order becomes paid and the payment becomes captured. The failure reason is captured as null; its previous value was uncaptured.
occurrences.narration: The payment is captured and the order becomes paid. A captured null failure reason means there is no failure. At the preceding occurrence that attribute was uncaptured.
One fulfillment work item is created for the paid order. The receipt is marked handled and HTTP 200 acknowledges the callback. The order is ready for packing.

scenarios.title: Repeated callback keeps one fulfillment
scenarios.description: In this synthetic example, the gateway retries event evt_481 after its payment and fulfillment work have been recorded. The service reads and verifies the handled receipt, then acknowledges the retry with HTTP 200. The paid order retains exactly one fulfillment item.

occurrences.narration: The gateway retries an already handled callback. The order is paid and one fulfillment item exists. The response status is not captured before this retry; null after receipt means no response has been sent for this request yet.

occurrences.changeSummary: The receipt lookup count increases from zero to one. The handled flag remains true.
occurrences.narration: The first lookup finds the handled receipt. This occurrence belongs to the first visit to Receipt checked. The lookup count becomes one.
The service takes the already-handled branch. It does not capture a second payment or enqueue a second fulfillment. A verification read will revisit Receipt checked.

occurrences.changeSummary: The receipt lookup count increases from one to two on this separate verification visit. The payment and fulfillment remain unchanged.
occurrences.narration: A second read verifies the saved receipt before acknowledgement. This is a separate occurrence at the same diagram node: its lookup count changes from one to two, not from zero to one.
HTTP 200 acknowledges the retry and stops further retries. The order remains paid, the payment remains captured, and exactly one fulfillment work item remains. No new work is created.

scenarios.title: Declined payment stops fulfillment
scenarios.description: In this synthetic example, the issuer declines the payment for pending order ORD-1043 because funds are insufficient. The service checks the new receipt, records the decline, and acknowledges the callback. The recording ends with a declined order and no fulfillment work.

occurrences.narration: The issuer sends a declined-payment callback for a different order, ORD-1043. The service records the incoming event before deciding which branch to take.
The receipt is new and unhandled. The issuer response is insufficient_funds, so this path takes the declined branch rather than capturing the payment.
The order and payment become declined. The failure reason is captured as insufficient_funds. The handled receipt gets HTTP 200; the failed payment is acknowledged without creating fulfillment work.

scenarios.title: First delivery closes fulfillment
scenarios.description: In this synthetic example, Rotterdam packs paid order ORD-1042 for Utrecht. DemoParcel collects and delivers the parcel on the first attempt. The queue closes the fulfillment item, while the order keeps a durable link to the delivered shipment.

occurrences.narration: Rotterdam packs the paid order for Utrecht with DemoParcel. The shipment is linked to the order and fulfillment work. Tracking is uncaptured; zero delivery attempts and null delivery and return metadata record a parcel awaiting pickup.

DemoParcel collects the parcel in Rotterdam for Utrecht and assigns NL-003488. Fulfillment becomes dispatched and the shipment becomes in_transit. Pickup is not a delivery attempt, so the count remains zero.

DemoParcel confirms delivery in Utrecht on the first attempt at 2026-10-09T14:32:00Z. The shipment becomes delivered with one attempt and no delivery issue. Fulfillment becomes complete; the order remains paid.

The queue removes the completed fulfillment work item and its links. The delivered shipment remains linked directly to the order as the durable delivery record. Absent after means the work item has been removed, not that its attributes became null.

scenarios.title: New payment exchange queues fulfillment
scenarios.description: This synthetic exchange follows a new authorized-payment callback between the gateway, payment service, receipt store, and fulfillment queue. Receipt verification permits capture and fulfillment. The recording ends with order ORD-1042 paid and one work item queued.

occurrences.narration: A callback arrives for order ORD-1042. The service creates a receipt for evt_481. No payment or fulfillment work has been completed yet.
The receipt has not been handled. The callback says the issuer authorized EUR 89.90, so this traversal takes the new-successful-callback branch.
The payment is captured and the order becomes paid. A captured null failure reason means there is no failure. At the preceding occurrence that attribute was uncaptured.
One fulfillment work item is created for the paid order. The receipt is marked handled and HTTP 200 acknowledges the callback. The order is ready for packing.

scenarios.title: Retry delivers the parcel
scenarios.description: In this synthetic example, DemoParcel cannot deliver the Utrecht parcel because the recipient is unavailable. The recipient schedules redelivery and the parcel revisits In transit before delivery on the second attempt. Closing fulfillment retains both attempts and the delivery timestamp on the shipment.

occurrences.narration: Rotterdam packs ORD-1042 for Utrecht with DemoParcel. The new shipment has zero delivery attempts and captured null delivery and return metadata. Tracking will be assigned at pickup.
DemoParcel collects the Utrecht parcel and assigns NL-003489. Fulfillment becomes dispatched and the shipment becomes in_transit. The carrier has not attempted delivery yet.

DemoParcel reaches Utrecht but the recipient is unavailable. The first attempt increments deliveryAttempts to one and records the delivery issue. The shipment becomes delivery_failed and fulfillment becomes exception; deliveredAt remains null.

The recipient arranges another delivery with DemoParcel. The parcel returns to In transit and fulfillment becomes dispatched. This separate visit retains one completed attempt and its issue; scheduling does not count as a second attempt.

DemoParcel delivers NL-003489 in Utrecht on the second attempt at 2026-10-10T14:32:00Z. The attempt count becomes two and the delivery issue clears to a captured null. Fulfillment becomes complete; return metadata remains null.

The queue acknowledges completed work and removes ful-31 with its links. The paid order retains its direct link to the delivered parcel, including both delivery attempts and the final delivery timestamp.

scenarios.title: Declined redelivery returns the parcel
scenarios.description: In this synthetic example, the recipient is unavailable for delivery and declines redelivery. DemoParcel returns the parcel to Rotterdam and the queue closes its fulfillment item. The order retains the returned shipment; this recording covers parcel handling and contains no refund event.

occurrences.narration: Rotterdam packs the paid order for Utrecht with DemoParcel. The shipment is created with zero attempts and null delivery and return metadata. The order and fulfillment links identify the parcel's work item.

DemoParcel picks up the parcel and assigns NL-003490 for Utrecht. The shipment becomes in_transit and fulfillment becomes dispatched. Delivery attempts remain zero because pickup does not reach the recipient.

The recipient is unavailable when DemoParcel attempts delivery in Utrecht. The shipment records one attempt and recipient unavailable, with status delivery_failed. Fulfillment becomes exception while delivery and return timestamps remain null.

The recipient declines redelivery, so DemoParcel returns NL-003490 to Rotterdam at 2026-10-10T10:18:00Z. Shipment and fulfillment become returned. The record keeps one attempt, its delivery issue, and returnReason redelivery declined; deliveredAt stays null.

The queue acknowledges the returned parcel and removes ful-31 with its links. The order keeps the returned shipment as a durable record. Payment status remains paid because this traversal records parcel handling, with no refund event.

scenarios.title: Repeated payment exchange keeps one fulfillment
scenarios.description: This synthetic exchange follows a gateway retry of handled event evt_481. The payment service reads the receipt twice through the verification loop, then acknowledges the duplicate. The existing payment and single fulfillment item remain intact.

occurrences.narration: The gateway retries an already handled callback. The order is paid and one fulfillment item exists. The response status is not captured before this retry; null after receipt means no response has been sent for this request yet.
The first lookup finds the handled receipt. This occurrence belongs to the first visit to Receipt checked. The lookup count becomes one.
The service takes the already-handled branch. It does not capture a second payment or enqueue a second fulfillment. A verification read will revisit Receipt checked.
A second read verifies the saved receipt before acknowledgement. This is a separate occurrence at the same diagram node: its lookup count changes from one to two, not from zero to one.
HTTP 200 acknowledges the retry and stops further retries. The order remains paid, the payment remains captured, and exactly one fulfillment work item remains. No new work is created.

scenarios.title: Declined payment exchange stops fulfillment
scenarios.description: This synthetic exchange follows an issuer-declined callback for order ORD-1043. The payment service verifies a new receipt and takes the insufficient-funds branch. The recording ends with the decline acknowledged and no fulfillment item created.

occurrences.narration: The issuer sends a declined-payment callback for a different order, ORD-1043. The service records the incoming event before deciding which branch to take.
The receipt is new and unhandled. The issuer response is insufficient_funds, so this path takes the declined branch rather than capturing the payment.
The order and payment become declined. The failure reason is captured as insufficient_funds. The handled receipt gets HTTP 200; the failed payment is acknowledged without creating fulfillment work.

scenarios.title: Authorized payment marks order paid
scenarios.description:
This synthetic detail recording expands payment capture for ORD-1042 into two actions. Payment pay-72 starts pending with an authorized amount of EUR 89.90. The service captures it, then marks the order paid.

Only the order and payment are captured here. Receipt acknowledgement and fulfillment queuing belong to the surrounding callback recording.

occurrences.narration:
The payment service captures the authorized EUR 89.90 on pay-72. The payment becomes captured and its failure reason is recorded as null.

The order is still pending in this intermediate snapshot. Marking the order paid is the next action in this detail recording.

With pay-72 captured, the service marks ORD-1042 paid. The order can now proceed to fulfillment.

This detail recording stops at the paid order. It does not record queuing, packing, or delivery.

scenarios.title: Captured payment marks the order paid
scenarios.description:
This synthetic sequence shows the payment service capturing pay-72 and then marking ORD-1042 paid. It expands the capture message from the callback sequence into the two domain operations.

The recording captures order and payment state only, and ends with a captured payment and paid order. The linked flow presents these operations as ordered actions.

occurrences.narration:
The payment service calls capture on pay-72 for the authorized EUR 89.90. The payment becomes captured with a null failure reason.

The order remains pending until the following message. The drill link opens the corresponding action flow, preserving this sequence visit.

After capture succeeds, the payment service calls markPaid on ORD-1042 with pay-72. The order changes from pending to paid while the captured payment retains its values.

The interaction ends here. Fulfillment belongs to the surrounding callback sequence.

scenarios.title: Priority order packed and dispatched
scenarios.description: In this synthetic example, a Rotterdam warehouse operator scans a priority packing request, prepares the workstation, and saves the dispatch work. The operator packs the parcel and prints its invoice and dispatch documents. Two recorded carrier checks retain separate snapshots. The recording ends after the carrier arrives and the dispatch notice is sent. Only one fulfillment work item is captured.

occurrences.narration: The warehouse receives a priority packing request. Work item ful-shape-demo is queued in Rotterdam.
The scanner reads the packing request. The input/output parallelogram marks data entering the workflow, and the work item becomes received.
The operator prepares the packing workstation. The preparation hexagon marks setup before processing the parcel.
The system saves the prepared dispatch work. The database cylinder describes persistent storage; the recorded work stage becomes stored.
The operator selects this work for expedited handling. The bottom-wide trapezoid marks prioritized work, and the captured stage becomes priority.
The operator packs and seals the parcel by hand. The top-wide trapezoid describes a human-performed operation, and the work item becomes packed.
The system creates one invoice for the packed parcel. The document shape describes that single sheet, and the work stage becomes invoiced.
The operator prints the invoice, packing slip, and carrier paperwork. Stacked document sheets describe the bundle, and the work becomes documentsReady.
The parcel and documents are ready, but the carrier has not arrived. The D-shaped delay marks this recorded wait, and the work becomes waiting.
A second check finds the carrier still pending. This separate occurrence revisits the same delay node with unchanged captured values.
The carrier arrives and the system sends the dispatch notice. The reversed input/output parallelogram describes outgoing data, and the work becomes notified.
The operator hands the prepared parcel to the carrier. The work item becomes dispatched, and the pill-shaped terminator marks the recording's completion.
